newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy third mobile phone licence on offer by June.
newsitem.headline: Italy third mobile phone licence on offer by June.

text.p: Italy will put its third licence to operate a mobile phone service up for tender by June, deputy posts and telecommunications minister Michele Lauria said on Thursday.

In a statement Lauria said Posts and Telecommunications Minister Antonio Maccanico had sent a draft of urgent measures to Prime Minister Romano Prodi establishing the procedure for the licence tender.
The measures, which are due to be examined by the cabinet as soon as possible, will allow the start of the tender by June, Lauria said.
"The government confirms its willingness to proceed quickly with the start of the tender for choosing the third mobile phone operator," the statement said.
The measures sent to Prodi also envisaged the introduction of a DECT (Digital European Cordless Telephony) supercordless telephone service for urban areas, it said.

Italy's third licence is to be for a PCN standard service and several companies have expressed interest already although some have complained that the government is taking a long time to offer the licence and allowing companies already operating mobile phone services to strengthen their position.
One group interested is Italian broadcaster Mediaset, part of former prime minister Silvio Berlusconi's Finivest media empire.
It is already partnering British Telecom and Italy's Banca Nazionale del Lavoro in joint Italian telecoms venture Albacom and together they intend to compete for the PCN licence.
An Italian newspaper reported this week that German telecoms giant Deutsche Telekom was also interested in competing in conjunction with Italian state electricity utility Enel.
While Enel did not confirm the report, saying it was talking to different parties, chairman Chicco Testa said it was no secret Enel was interested in entering the sector.
Italy currently has two GSM standard mobile phone service operators, state-controlled Telecom Italia Mobile (TIM) and Olivetti-controlled Omnitel Pronto Italia.
Both companies are also interested in DECT technology and Italy's state-controlled fixed line operator Telecom Italia said last year it wanted to set up its own DECT service.
